messages:
maria: Heads up — after landing the CUDA-graph capture for the attention kernels we saw an 18% end-to-end throughput regression on the 16-GPU tensor+pipeline config for long sequences (8k). Timeline shows compute stalls while all-reduce queues up. attaching quick profile extract below.

maria: nsight snippet (simplified):
```
TIME    STREAM  ACTIVITY
0.00ms  S0      kernel(attn_fwd)
0.40ms  S1      all_reduce(start)
0.42ms  S0      idle (waiting event)
0.90ms  S1      all_reduce(end)
0.91ms  S0      kernel(attn_bwd)
```
seems like the compute stream is waiting on an event from the comm stream but the event isn't fired until graph replay finishes.

diego: can repro locally on a dev box with 4xA100 in pipeline+tensor mode, same behaviour. interestingly, single-GPU runs are fine.

sam: do we capture the comm ops inside the CUDA graph? iirc we only capture kernels on the compute stream; NCCL ops are launched on the comm stream outside capture which can break ordering.

maria: right — our current capture flow: capture compute stream work into graph, replay graph, then enqueue NCCL allreduce on comm stream. I think the graph's replay is blocking the event that signals comm progress because of stream semantics when graphs are involved.

rachel: recall CUDA graphs can serialize work when you mix stream-ordered memory ops and events. If the graph was captured with implicit syncpoints, replay can prevent comm stream from progressing until graph completes.

diego: quick code snippet of capture pattern we're using: 
```cpp
cudaStream_t s_compute = streams[compute_idx];
cudaStreamBeginCapture(s_compute, cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal);
launch_attention_forward(..., s_compute);
cudaStreamEndCapture(s_compute, &graph);
cudaGraphInstantiate(&inst, graph, NULL, NULL, 0);
// replay per batch
cudaGraphLaunch(inst, s_compute);
// then enqueue NCCL on comm stream
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
```
Looks innocent but with stream-ordered memory traffic the replay may implicitly insert syncs.

sam: two hypotheses: (1) graph replay serializes against the comm stream because of captured host-device memcopies or events; (2) our kernel selection changed and we now pick a fused kernel that runs longer and delays the point where the KV-cache is exposed to comms. either could increase overlap sensitivity.

maria: kernel selection note — infra-bot just rolled the new kernel-selector rules in yesterday's runtime build (build 2026.03.16). perf-bot flagged a regression in a separate smoke test but it was marked non-blocking.

perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression: attention-latency increased 12% on nightly 2026.03.16 (job: nightly/inference-longseq).

rachel: can we try launching NCCL ops inside the same captured graph (i.e., capture comm stream work by calling ncclCommEnqueue?) I think NCCL supports enqueuing kernels to streams within a capture if you use the CUDA graph API for NCCL ops. but that's brittle w.r.t versions.

diego: tried capturing enqueueing NCCL via cudaGraphAddMemcpyNode trick and it deadlocked in CI. also saw a cudaErrorNotSupported on older drivers.

sam: alternate: add explicit event after graph launch on compute stream and make comm stream wait on that event before launching all-reduce, but that reverses the desired ordering (we want compute to signal comm to start earlier).

maria: we added an event post-kernel earlier to try to force overlap; timeline then shows two events but the graph replay doesn't advance compute stream progress sufficiently for the event to be recorded in time.

rachel: another angle — KV cache handling: we use peer-to-peer transfers between GPUs for KV sharding. If graphs capture the device-to-device memcpy semantics differently, the cache flush/attach point may be pushed later too, delaying the point where comm can operate on fresh KV buffers.

maria: repro checklist I'm running:
- reproduce locally with `--model=redwood-7b --seq_len=8192 --parallel=tp4_pp4`
- run with nsight timeline and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` (so we can see async ordering)
- toggle new kernel-selector off to isolate kernel selection impact
- try capturing NCCL inside the graph vs outside with different event wiring

sam: for profiling, also record cudaProfilerStart/cudaProfilerStop around the replay region and collect CUPTI activity. CUPTI traces helped me find an event insertion we didn't expect in a previous incident.

diego: quick data point: with kernel-selector disabled, regression drops to ~4% but doesn't fully vanish. suggests both kernel duration + graph semantics contribute.

maria: plan: (1) test fallback where we disable graph capture for long-seq path and measure; (2) if disabling recovers perf, iterate on capturing NCCL (if supported) or change ordering to capture both compute+comm in the same graph; (3) add runtime guard to disable graph capture on mixed-stream topologies until validated.

rachel: +1. also add a small litmus test in infra that runs tensor+pipeline combined with graph capture to catch reintroductions. put a driver-version matrix too.

sam: I'll prototype a variant that issues an early pinned memcpy host->device as a captureable marker to force the graph to include the dependency and see if that helps overlap.

maria: thanks — if anyone has prior patch notes or driver-version quirks around `cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal` and NCCL please paste them here. I'm going to open an incident ticket after we confirm root cause.

perf-bot: [note] rolled back runtime build 2026.03.16 for nightly/inference-longseq to 2026.03.15.

infra-bot: reminder — if you capture NCCL ops with CUDA graphs, ensure NCCL version >= 2.14 and CUDA >= 12.2 per vendor notes.

diego: pinned a small repro in /mnt/dev/repros/1764211200-graph-comm-deadlock, includes nsight traces and a capture-mode toggle.

maria: awesome, @diego please add a short README with exact driver/kernel versions that reproduce. I'll triage with QA and schedule a quick sync if we need a hotfix.

sam: FYI I also saw a similar pattern with KV cache eviction when we use GPUDirect for P2P — eviction op was blocked until graph finished and that introduced jitter. might be related.

rachel: ok closing loop: short-term fallback disable graphs for TP+PP long sequences; mid-term either capture comms or redesign capture pipeline to ensure visibility ordering; long-term add kernel-selector perf tests and CI gating.

maria: thanks all, will file incident and link this thread.
